summary: Read-only M7/M8 readiness run completed. Executed requested isolated backend suites (excluding process_recovery_mongo per isolation rule), added public authenticated portal/API regression tests against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, and validated /os/admin/rulesupd + /dap/entitlement at 1920x800 and 390x844. Confirmed both RMS and DIGICOW operators have resolved licence with zero listed catalog rows; billing endpoint is mounted and readable.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout contract not enforced: 6 wrong-password attempts still return 401 and immediate correct login still succeeds (no 5-fail lockout).

State transition to EFFECTIVE occurs in state_machine before emit_countersign_ledger_row in router; ledger-write failure can leave effective state without matching ledger row (non-atomic ceremony/evidence split).
RuleChangeRequest model/state machine has no tenant_id and collection access is request_id-only, creating cross-tenant collision/isolation risk for deterministic IDs.

minor.issue: App auth does not set an application session cookie (only bearer token in JSON TokenPair; observed Set-Cookie was Cloudflare bot cookie).
Response header included access-control-allow-origin: * on POST response path (edge behavior), while credentialed CORS should remain explicit-origin only.
Seeder is create-only and does not update existing admin password when changed, so seed_admin update-idempotency contract is not satisfied.

integration_issues.issue: Page is explicitly HONEST-GAP surface only (backend not wired). This is a functional journey gap, not a rendering defect.

action_items: Implement/verify auth lockout after 5 failed login attempts per playbook.
Make checker transition + ledger emission atomic (or compensating rollback) so EFFECTIVE cannot exist without evidence row.
Add tenant scoping to checker request persistence/queries and deterministic ID conflict boundary.
Decide whether auth transport remains bearer-only or needs first-party httpOnly cookie flow; align tests/docs accordingly.
Verify ingress/proxy CORS header rewriting on credentialed auth responses so wildcard origin is never emitted on protected flows.
If required by milestone contract, connect rules_update_lifecycle apply/recheck outputs to effective policy publication path.
critical_code_review_comments: rules_service.rule_registry is process-local singleton with in-memory append-only state; no durable/shared publication semantics at this layer.
approvals.rules_update_lifecycle persists countdown/apply/recheck files but does not itself publish effective runtime rule policy.
business_continuity anchors pin 3600s and continuity attestations, but continuity module is attestation-only; restore execution path is not implemented in this service.
n_series.breach writes realtime alert files for DPO/witness and stores receipt paths, but no delivery-consumer/acknowledgement loop is present in inspected runtime paths.

success_rate.backend: 100% on executed requested suites (91/91) + 10/10 public-read tests; 1 skipped cross-tenant retained-id check due no retained census rows exposed; process_recovery_mongo intentionally not executed

seed_data_creation: None. No user/account seeding, no production/preview business-record writes, no rule/apply commission actions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Process-recovery test file (/app/backend/tests/execution_spine/test_process_recovery_mongo.py) was skipped because it uses shared configured Mongo DB_NAME rather than an isolated temporary database. Public API read-only suite asserts: both operators login/me=200, unauthenticated refusals, entitlement licence resolved + catalog count 0 for RMS and DIGICOW, billing endpoint 200. Cross-tenant retained-ID read check is present but skipped when /api/portal/census/records has no rows.
rca of the issue: Auth lockout gap RCA: router/auth + user_store implement stateless credential verification with no failed-attempt counter, lock timestamp, or denylist path, so repeated failures never transition account/session into lockout state. Checker atomicity RCA: router calls state_machine.countersign() first (persisting EFFECTIVE), then separately emits ledger row; any post-state ledger failure causes state/evidence divergence.
